items.issueTitle: R-0001 Review the redrafted articles and corrected studies

feedback.message: Wrote notes/R-0001.md. Verdict: neither piece ready for the keeper yet. Must fix in the xz record and article: the March valgrind errors were silenced by the attacker's 5.6.1, which Freund and the Cox timeline both say; the uptake was lobbied, not uncoordinated; Debian carried the backdoor about a month, not some days; the figure needs the same. Must fix in the survey: the claim that no source can tell which crawls came from AI contradicts the crawler window, and Cloudflare groups crawlers by purpose; the illustration draws the overlap the record says is unmeasured, and its alt text contradicts its caption. Seven should-fix and four notes. All findings of the first review were carried into the text. Six fetches used. Committed as 4a2e5cf.

E-0004 Correct LH003 and redraft its article. First the record: in studies/LH003/, add a Corrections section entry dated today citing notes/review-2026-09-26-first-articles.md, and amend the text and table so that (a) 'almost disjoint by construction' is replaced by partial views whose relationships are unmeasured, acknowledging the connections the table itself records, such as deps.dev joining package ecosystems, forge projects and OSV advisories; (b) the table gains two columns, publication date and observation window, beside the date read, filled where the source states them and blank with a note where it does not; (c) the Anthropic Economic Index row is dated to the report it describes and says that later reports widened the scope; (d) the statement that no source observes propagation directly is restated as Lighthouse's classification, with the empirical question being which records support identifying and testing such relationships. Then the piece: redraft articles/what-we-can-see.md from the corrected record under the piece rules in AGENTS.md, opening with the question a reader actually has, one idea, provenance in the notes, no internal references, ending on the joint-sample question, with a colophon in the LH F05 piece form; draw the illustration as a plain SVG at articles/what-we-can-see-map.svg with a one-line caption. Done when the record is corrected and the piece reads aloud without tripping. This will let us explain what the existing observatories reveal and what they cannot. Follow one concrete question, could we count how much AI activity happens on the internet, and let each source contribute something to the attempted answer. For the voice, this is the target for the passage about what stays unobserved: a model running on someone's own computer may never appear in a broker's usage figures; its absence from that chart tells us where the broker's view ends, and nothing about whether the model is doing something harmful.

Work in the repository at /home/user/lighthouse. Follow AGENTS.md there. Commit the deliverable. When finished, report what you did, what could not be done, and the files you changed.
